A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Planar Symmetric Pattern Generation and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–G. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial appendix revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original pattern-generation comparisons, topology and metamaterial simulations, and a fabricated paper-cutting example in Section 6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including CLIP-A scores, symmetry errors, mechanical-performance distributions and fabrication examples.

M1.justification: Section 5.2 corrects the stated mask density from 1 minus sigmoid to sigmoid, reversing the solid/void assignment to match the void-color definition. The core symmetrization algorithm, invariant bases and optimization pipeline remain unchanged; an implementation change or rerun is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four applications, including all 17 pattern symmetries, four paper-cutting groups and the first 12 planar groups for metamaterials. Changing the introductory count from three to four applications corrects the description of existing coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, basis projection, Zhong et al.'s CLIP-based topology method and DDIM in their corresponding experiments. The new FFT discussion does not add an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 6.3 withdraws the claim of identical hyperparameters; both appendices already report 401 baseline versus 801 proposed-method optimization steps. Section 6.4 now labels the error as relative volume-fraction MAE, and F.2 changes the written p2mm prompt from 'red Chinese paper cutting, lantern' to 'x Chinese paper cutting, lantern'. These are reported-protocol revisions, without evidence of reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix F.3 adds a brief qualitative comparison of topology optimization using SD 2.1 versus SDXL void-color encodings. No quantitative ablation accompanies it. Existing resolution/basis-fraction tests, symmetry-error analyses and fabrication examples are retained.

E5.justification: The same generated-sample distributions are reported, with no added seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The revised phrase 'in the reported runs' supplies no new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Numerical tables and result figures are retained: for example, Table 1 still reports proposed-method scores of 4.30, 4.20 and 3.99. Appendix F.3 newly states that SD 2.1-derived void encodings outperform their SDXL counterparts, but provides no numerical comparison.

T1.justification: Appendices B–E substantially replace embedding, invariant-ring, module-rank and connectivity proofs. Higher-dimensional nonembedding statements are narrowed to linear conjugacy; C.12 is generalized conditionally to R^n, C.13 is added, and E.3 gains explicit boundary and finite-component assumptions. Basis, index and coordinate derivations are corrected, while the alternative Fourier derivation in D.3 is removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: continuous representations with arbitrary planar-group symmetry, their approximation capability, and symmetry-controlled generation across four design applications.

C2.justification: v2 replaces guaranteed connectivity from the optimization strategy with connectivity promotion, qualifies unnormalized mechanical comparisons as valid within the same lattice setting, and describes metamaterial mechanics as diffusion-prior guidance. It also corrects the dimensional applicability discussion and acknowledges efficient FFT projection instead of treating expensive QR computation as intrinsic to basis projection.

D1.justification: Appendices F and G add specific resolutions, the metamaterial hash-grid range, lattice lengths/angles/origins, the SD 2.1 encoder used for the void latent, and implementation through skew reflections for oblique groups. These supplement existing implementation descriptions; the code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The theoretical bibliography adds Humphreys (2000) and removes sources including Artin (2011), Tahara (1971) and Shmueli (2010), accompanying replaced or deleted derivations. The principal positioning against earlier generation and topology-design work remains.

P1.justification: Appendices B–E undergo extensive rewriting and restructuring of their explanations, including removal of D.3. Sections 3.3 and 5–6 are also revised for clarity and qualification. This exceeds local copyediting, although the main section order remains.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables are retained, with revised captions and local layout changes. Table 1 explicitly identifies the p1 setting, and the topology galleries now follow the metamaterial-details section. Plot content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the mathematical support for the paper: C.3 replaces unsupported general real-polynomial descent with an explicit invariant-generator construction, C.10 handles differing translation lattices, and E.3 supplies additional assumptions and a replacement connectivity proof. Corrected mask semantics, clearer implementation details and qualified comparison claims reinforce these gains. Although the alternative Fourier derivation is removed and quantitative experiments are unchanged, the repairs address important deficiencies in the justification of the central method.
